tossups.text: This element attacks bromine in a reaction that converts one functional group with this element to another, the Hofmann rearrangement. The Sandmeyer reaction is driven by the leaving of a functional group containing two atoms of this element. An atom of this element in potassium phthalimide attacks a primary alkyl halide to form a functional group with this element bonded to carbon in the Gabriel synthesis. This element can be protonated when bonded to three other groups to give a quaternary salt. This element is triple bonded to carbon in the cyano group and is bonded to three methyl groups in a molecule that gives fish their distinct smell. For 10 points, name this element bonded to carbon in amides and amines with atomic number 7.

A group of cells in the nucleus basalis of Meynert produce this compound. Neostigmine is used as a treatment for myasthenia gravis because of its ability to increase the levels of this compound. Sarin binds to this compound's namesake esterase, preventing its decomposition in the synaptic cleft and triggering repeated action potentials. This neurotransmitter consists of an ester of a quaternary ammonium compound and a two carbon carboxylic acid. Black widow venom stimulates the release of this neurotransmitter, while botulin suppresses it. For 10 points, name this neurotransmitter released at neuromuscular junctions to stimulate contractions.

Anegada is the northernmost island in this archipelago, as well as the only one of non-volcanic origin. The Soggy Dollar Bar is a well known tourist destination on this archipelago's island of Jost Van Dyke, which is about five miles from another member, Tortola. The southernmost island in this archipelago is also the largest and has residents who refer to themselves as Crucians. Split between the US and Great Britain, For 10 points, what is this archipelago which includes St. John, St. Thomas, and St. Croix [croy].

Within this region, 10,000 year-old human remains and artifacts have been excavated at its Gobero site. This region's Toubou [TOO-boo] people live in its Tibesti Mountains. Lake Chad is the only freshwater lake in this region. The Sahel forms a transition zone between this desert and the tropical savannas to the south, and to the north are the Atlas Mountains. For ten points, name this desert in north Africa, the largest hot desert in the world.

A feast for this religious figure in mid-August is prepared for by a two-week fast. It's not Artemis, but a "House of" this figure stands a few miles outside Ephesus. This figure, who caused the "Miracle of the Sun" near Fátima in 1917, is the subject of the fourth and fifth Glorious Mysteries, and a request including the phrase "now and at the hour of our death". This subject of the writing Ineffabilis Deus is called "Theotokos" by Orthodox churches. This figure underwent the Dormition before the Assumption, and was free of original sin due to the Immaculate Conception. For 10 points, name this woman who is "full of grace," the husband of Joseph and mother of Jesus.

This academic discussed a conflict with the Kahama in what was described as the "Four Year War." Important subjects studied by this individual include Gigi, Goliath, and David Greybeard. This individual's earliest research focused on the Kasakela group, who she observed hunting colobus monkeys. This individual was one of the first to describe affectionate behavior in her subjects' family group and she was also one of the first to describe a "fishing" like behavior in which her subjects used sticks or reeds to harvest termites. This woman got started in her field thanks to her correspondence with Louis Leakey. Most of her work was done at Gombe River National Park. For ten points, name this English primatologist, most notable for studying chimpanzees.

Because specific variants of this protein are often named after the geographic location in which they are discovered, its variants include Yakima and Kansas, each of which lacks a hydrogen bond that stabilizes one of its two stable quaternary states. Though the Adair and Hill equations are generally used for any enzyme, they were developed in studies of this protein. Max Perutz discovered the structure of this protein. A glutamate to valine mutation in this protein leads to its S variant, found in sickle-cell anemia. This protein has a higher affinity for carbon monoxide than its more biologically necessary substrate. For 10 points, name this protein that binds to up to four oxygen molecules and carries it through the bloodstream.

By depicting this place, an artist sought to make a preceding style "solid and durable, like the art of museums" and "redo Poussin entirely from nature," as in a painting bisected by a viaduct. Joachim Gasquet's books on Asian art inspired paintings of this place, beginning with 1870's The Railway Cutting. This is likely where an artist spent "entire days... reading Virgil and looking at the sky," as recounted by his admirer Paul Gauguin. The artist's blocky "constructive stroke" was often used for landscapes of this place "seen from" Bellevue, Bibemus Quarry, and Les Lauves ("lay LOHV"). During his final years in Aix-en-Provence ("ex on pro-VAWNS"), a Post-Impressionist artist painted this place from many angles and times of day, along with large paintings of Bathers. For 10 points, what mountain was a frequent subject of Paul Cézanne?

A speaker who lists challenges for this activity declares "My advice is-give it up!" in Gerard Nolst Trenité's poem "The Chaos," which opens Arika Okrent's book Highly Irregular. Programs that assist this activity are susceptible to the Cupertino effect. In 1990, former Portuguese colonies signed a treaty to regulate this activity, which Germany reformed in 1996 to standardize the Eszett ("ess-TSETT"). William Barfée uses his "magic foot" to triumph at this activity in a William Finn musical set in Putnam County. "Blue-backed" books taught this activity, whose simplification was the goal of a board supported by Teddy Roosevelt and Andrew Carnegie. Indian-American kids dominate a competitive form of this activity run by Scripps. For 10 points, what activity often requires an extra letter U in British English?
acceptableAnswers: accept The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee

tossups.text: Old World primates and guinea pigs have lost the ability to synthesize this compound. Foods rich in this substance are called antiscorbutics [anti-skor-byoo-tiks]. Nobel laureate Linus Pauling advocated taking mega-doses of this compound to prevent the common cold. This compound is needed by the body to build collagen, so its deficiency will result in scurvy. For 10 points, name this vitamin concentrated in citrus fruits like limes and oranges.

An eponymous algorithm that shares its name with these structures swaps two elements every step to generate all permutations of a set. Cartesian trees that apply a property named for these structures to their priorities are very similar to randomized binary search trees. Generalized examples of these structures are called "d-ary"("D-air-ee"). The decrease-key operation on these structures is used in Prim's algorithm and Dijkstra's algorithm, which can be sped up using the "Fibonacci" type as a priority queue. A "big O of n log n" sorting algorithm repeatedly removes the root of this structure and "sifts" to find the next largest element. For 10 points, the "max" type of what structures enforce that parents are larger than their children?

This poem concludes with a speaker who hopes that he "blazed a trail" for "more versatile singers" in the "rising younger generation." This poem's reliance on stock epithets is exemplified by its repeated description of the main character as "steadfast old." This poem makes frequent use of parallel repetitions within verses, as in its opening lines, "It is my desire / It is my wish / to set out to sing, / to begin to recite." This poem's "old" edition was updated fifteen years later with material gathered by David Europaeus, including a tragic "cycle" about an orphan who kills himself after sleeping with a maiden who turns out to be his sister. This poem's main character sails away aboard a copper raft in its fiftieth and final section, or runo. This poem's use of trochaic tetrameter inspired Henry Wadsworth Longfellow to do the same in his Song of Hiawatha. For 10 points, Elias Lönnrot compiled stories about Lemminkäinen and Väinämöinen into what Finnish epic?

The United Kingdom uses the TORRO scale to measure the intensity of these events. In the US, the damage caused by these events is used to rank them on an "Enhanced" scale, named for Ted Fujita, that tops out at F5. A "freight train" noise commonly accompanies, for 10 points, what natural disasters that can include three hundred mile-per-hour winds and a rotating funnel cloud of debris?

A holder of this position choked protestor Bill Clennett in the "Shawinigan ("sha-WIN-ni-ghen") Handshake." A holder of this position was accused of accepting kickbacks from Karlheinz Schreiber in the Airbus affair. Bidding on railroad contracts led to the downfall of the first holder of this position in the Pacific Scandal. A holder of this position instituted the War Measures Act after the FLQ kidnapped James Cross and Pierre Laporte in the October Crisis. Brian Mulroney held this position, as did a man who defeated Stephen Harper in a 2015 election. For 10 points, name this position currently held by Justin Trudeau ("tru-DOE").
acceptableAnswers: other official titles that are not Prime Minister

tossups.text: The effective potential energy surface felt by nuclei according to the Born-Oppenheimer approximation are sometimes called surfaces of this type. A transition of this type, in which a system retains its eigenstate of the initial Hamiltonian, cannot occur when the Landau-Zener velocity is zero, according to a theorem of this name. This term also describes a type of lapse rate associated with an air mass that expands to attain lower atmospheric pressures. An effect which is used to achieve temperatures on the order of millikelvins involves removing the magnetic field from a highly ordered paramagnet, and is called this type of "magnetization," while the "index" of this type is the ratio of heat capacity at constant pressure and heat capacity at constant temperature. For 10 points, identify this term which also describes a process in which heat is not transferred to or from the system.

This term first appears in Sextio-Licinian laws of 367, when this office was stripped of the power to conduct trials. Charged with summoning the Senate, proposing laws to the people, and presiding over elections, they always had the task of conducting important foreign wars as the superior holders of imperium, ranking above the Praetors. For 10 points, name this fourth rung of the cursus honorum, the chief executive magistracy and most powerful elected office in Republican Rome, usually occupied by two men.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for pancreas digestive enzymes. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this liver-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The liver is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in pancreas digestive enzymes.

tossups.text: In one poem, this character wonders why a woman neglects him after he gave her chameleons and a "harmless snake" "disarmèd of its teeth and sting." Later in that poem, this character hurts himself and bemoans, "Alas! These hurts are slight" compared to "those that die by love's despite." In another poem, this man states that (+) "the gods themselves with us do dwell" after claiming that "another world was searched" "to find the Marvel of Peru." That poem begins with this character asserting that "luxurious man" seduced nature where it "was most plain and pure." In a different poem, this character addresses some creatures whose "officious flame" goes to waste as his mind is displaced with the thoughts of a woman. In this character's "Song," he repeats a couplet stating that Juliana comes, and "she, what I do to the grass, does to my thoughts and me." For 10 points, name this field worker who addresses "the Glow-Worms" in one of four poems written by Andrew Marvell.

In a photograph taken by Oscar Graubner, this artist can be seen perched atop the sixty-one story gargoyle of the Chrysler Building. One work by this artist depicts a happy family in a car on a billboard with the text "World's Highest Standard of Living" and "There's No Way Like the American Way," which it contrasts with a bread line below. She depicted the suicide of Leipzig mayor Dr. Lisso and his family and the Buchenwald concentration camp in a series begun before the end of World War II. With her husband Erskine Caldwell, she photographed the American south for the collection "You Have Seen Their Faces." For 10 points, name this American photographer and war correspondent who was commissioned by Life Magazine to take a picture of Gandhi at his spinning wheel shortly before his death.

This general organized a mass wedding at Susa. This general's conquests ended when their troops refused to cross the Beas (bee-YASS) River despite a victory at the battle of the Hydaspes. This ruler named a city after their horse, Bucephalus. This leader of the Companion Cavalry defeated a revolt by Thebes against this general's father. After this ruler's death, their empire was divided up by the Diadochi,(dye-AD-o-kye), which included Ptolemy and Seleucus.(sell-YOU-cuss). This general was undefeated in battles like Issus during their conquest of the Persian Achaemenid(a-KEE-ma-nid) Empire. For 10 points, name this "great" king of Macedon.

parts.text: First, name this small difference between the 2-S and 2-P energy levels of the hydrogen atom arising from virtual phonons interacting with the electron.

The measuring the energy difference from the Lamb can result in an accurate measurement of the fine structure constant and therefore can be used as an accurate precision test for this SU1.) gauge theory that involves the quantization of fields produced by charged particles.
Often used in QED and quantum field theories is this theorem, which states that a product of ladder operators can be decomposed into a sum of products of pairs of said operators.

bonuses.leadin: This energy correction is proportional to the fine structure constant to the fifth power and was measured by Hans Bethe in the hydrogen atom in 1947. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this so-called function that is useful in modeling unit impulses. It returns a value of infinity when the input is zero, though its integral from negative to positive infinity is one.
In all other cases, the Dirac delta function returns this value. For a body in equilibrium, this is the value of the net force acting on the body.

Integrating the Dirac Delta function is possible since one can assign this value to subsets of the Dirac Delta function. Assigning this quantity to a set is necessary in order to perform Lebesgue integration over the set.

bonuses.leadin: This function is not really a function, but rather a distribution, and it is a continuous analogue of a similar function named for Kronecker. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this pass where the Afridi tribe of one group have long exercised the right of toll for those crossing the Spin Ghar mountains.

Home to one of Europe's many 'Devil's Bridges', which was painted by Turner, this Alpine pass has now been repeatedly bypassed by exceptionally long tunnels. The most recent of them, the 'Base Tunnel', vastly reduced travel time between Zürich and Milan.
Migrants travelling on this route crossed the Rocky Mountains through the South Pass. The final goal of many migrants on this route was Willamette Valley in its namesake northwestern state.

bonuses.leadin: Forts along this pass include Ali Masjid, and its highest point is at Landi Kotal, the namesake terminus of a no-longer-functional railway safari. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this boy who thwarted Saint Dane on Cloral, and in a later adventure saves the Bantu from an apocalyptic flood.
Containing works like The Quillian Games and Raven Rise, the Pendragon series was penned by this British author who also produced the T.V. series Flight 29 Down.
This character from the series betrayed the travelers and joined Saint Dane. In The Quillian Games she betrays Bobby and helps destroy Mr. Pop.

bonuses.leadin: In one adventure this boy's adversary disguises himself as Po Nassi and he convinces Ty Manoo to create a fertilizer that turns crops to poison. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this German philosopher who described the categorical imperative in his Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals.
Kant published the Prolegomena to Any Future Metaphysics as a clarification to this work, in which he demonstrates the existence of synthetic a priori truths.
In the Critique of Pure Reason, Kant distinguishes between phenomena and these imperceptible things that he calls "things-in-themselves."

bonuses.leadin: In one work, this philosopher envisions a "kingdom of ends" and argues that we should be able to will the maxim by which we act to be a universal law. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Standardizing this Chinese character set, which has fewer characters and strokes than its "traditional" counterpart, was a component of government literacy initiatives in China during the twentieth century.
During the nineteenth century, Romania replaced its writing system, which used this alphabet, with its current Latin-based alphabet, exchanging many Slavic words in favor of Romance ones.

When they exist, these organizations that govern grammar, pronunciation, and word meanings are typically considered authoritative over their languages. A "Royal" one of these institutions oversees the Spanish language.

bonuses.leadin: Language reform is the process of making widespread changes to a language's vocabulary, grammar, or spelling. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Peaking in incidence in early adulthood, this cancer is staged according to the Ann Arbor classification system, which is based on the number and location of affected lymph nodes. It is characterized by the presence of Reed-Sternberg cells which, under microscopy, look kind of like owls.

This extremely rapidly growing tumor, another form of lymphoma, though rare in the developed world outside of the immunosuppressed patient population, is common in children from malarial regions. It is linked to Epstein-Barr viral infection, and it is characterized microscopically as having a "starry sky" appearance.

Primarily afflicting the elderly, this cancer is often a progression from a myeloproliferative or myelodysplastic syndrome, and is distinguishable by having a greater than 20% or 30% blast involvement of the blood or bone marrow.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, identify these highly treatable acute hematological malignancies.

parts.text: Name this opera in which Judith ends up on the wrong side of the last door.
Duke Bluebeard's Castle was an opera by this composer of Mikrokosmos.
This is the initial aesthetic reason Judith gives for insisting that Duke Bluebeard's doors be opened.
acceptableAnswers: accept anything having to do with getting more light

bonuses.leadin: A blood-stained torture chamber, an armory, a beautiful garden, and a group of ex-wives are among the things Judith finds behind the doors in this opera. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this country located in the eastern Caucasus Mountains, with capital at Baku.
Stepanakert [step-uh-nuh-KERT] is the capital of this hyphenated Armenian enclave that is located within the borders of Azerbaijan.
Armenia and Azerbaijan are both directly north of this country, which is home to the Elbruz and Zagros mountains. Cities in this country include Tabriz, Esfahan, and its capital, Tehran.

bonuses.leadin: This country is home to Heydar Aliyev International Airport, and its capital city is located on the Absheron peninsula, which extends into the Caspian Sea. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this term, which also describes the seasonal movements of organisms, such as the Canadian goose, which flies south during the winter.
Migration in genetics requires this type of genetic drift to occur. A subtype of bottleneck, this event happens when a small group of individuals forms a new population.
Seasonal migration has been extensively in these insects, which fly from Canada to Mexico each year. The Viceroy butterfly mimics this species.

bonuses.leadin: This term is used to describe gene flow in population genetics, where it occurs when individuals move from one population to another. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this data type whose searching is analogized to "finding a needle in a haystack." Regular expressions are used to match patterns in this data type.
This string-searching algorithm uses a rolling hash called its namesake "fingerprint" to quickly filter out mismatches, thus achieving linear time matching.
Algorithms that give approximate answers to string searching are sometimes described by this term. A form of logic described by this term allows truth values between 0 and 1.

bonuses.leadin: The "bad-character" and "good-suffix" rules are used when implementing the Boyer-Moore algorithm for searching this data type. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Germanic god often depicted on skis carrying a bow.
Ydalir was considered a part of Alfheim, which was ruled by this Vanir god. His possessions include the golden boar Gullinbursti and the foldable ship Skidbladnir.
Because he had earlier relinquished his sword in an effort to woo Gerd, Frey was easily killed by the jotun Surt wrath during this final apocalyptic battle of Norse mythology.

bonuses.leadin: This god's home is called Ydalir and he is considered the daughter of Sif and the stepson of Thor. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this wide, flat bundle of neural fibers beneath the cortex.
The corpus callosum is a type of this tissue. These tissues transmit signals between regions of the cerebrum and are clinically evaluated with Diffusion Tensor Imaging.

White matter is characterized by this lipid dielectric which insulates the axons. Schwann cells supply the peripheral neurons with these structures and gaps between them along the axon are called nodes of Ranvier.

bonuses.leadin: This part of the brain connects the left and right hemispheres. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Hunyadi was born in this modern-day Romanian region. Another leader who ruled over this Wallachian region would famously stake his enemies' heads on poles.
After the Long Campaign, Hunyadi served as Regent-Governor of this country, his homeland, where he governed from Budapest.
This son of Hunyadi consolated the Hungarian realm after he was elected King. The Black Army was led by this ruler, who was nicknamed for the raven on his sigil.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about "Christ's Champion," the late medieval warlord John Hunyadi, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this construct that describes a system in thermal equilibrium with a heat bath at fixed temperature. It is characterized by the number of particles, the absolute temperature, and the volume.

The distribution of states in the canonical ensemble is named for either Josiah Willard Gibbs or this Austrian inventor of statistical mechanics, who also names the constant k-sub-B that appears in the distribution.

The [emphasize] microcanonical ensemble describes identical physics to the canonical ensemble, but considers a collection of microstates in which this quantity, rather than temperature, is held constant.

bonuses.leadin: The occupation probability for a microstate in this system is equal to the negative exponential of the state's energy over k-sub-B times T, all divided by the partition function. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this leader whose tenure was mired by the Bofors scandal and the Shah Bano case. This man succeeded his mother as prime minister of his country after she was assassinated in 1984.

Rajiv Gandhi was himself assassinated in 1991 by a member of this group. Velupillai Prabhakaran founded this militant group, which fought the majority-Sinhalese government during the Sri Lankan Civil War.
Another crisis during Gandhi's tenure was the Bhopal disaster, which involved a chemical leak at a plant producing these substances. DDT was one of these substances used against mosquitos.

bonuses.leadin: In response to ongoing riots, this politician said, "when a mighty tree falls, it is only natural that the earth around it does shake a little." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with gastric secretions.
What is the main function of the esophagus in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to gastric secretions.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.

parts.text: Name this author of "The Ballad of the Harp-Weaver" and the one-act play Aria da Capo.

In this Millay poem, the narrator describes how "Into the earth sank I / Full six feet under ground did lie." She begins to die, but, after realizing she will never see the sky again, prays to God to be reborn.

This Millay sonnet states that only one Greek has directly observed the titular figure, while others "stare at nothing, intricately drawn nowhere" and a few fortunate ones "have heard her massive sandal set on stone".
parts.answer: “Euclid alone has looked on Beauty bare”
acceptableAnswers: “Euclid alone has looked on Beauty bare”
The “Euclid alone has looked on Beauty bare”

parts.text: Identify this jazz composition that begins with "So What".
This jazz pioneer and trumpeter created Kind of Blue and the album Sketches of Spain.
Jimmy Cobb played this instrument in Davis' sextet on Kind of Blue. Other famous jazz musicians who played this instrument include Elvin Jones and Gene Krupa.

bonuses.leadin: This album contains the track "Freddie Freeloader" which featured a double bass solo by Paul Chambers. For 10 points each:

parts.text: He gained prominence during the English Civil War as one of the commanders of the New Model Army. He would go on to govern, from 1653 to 1658, as Lord Protector of .

Cromwell saw his star rise after his cavalry defeated that of Prince Rupert's in this July 1644 battle which saw Thomas Fairfax make an early evening attack on Royalist Forces eventually leading to the capture of York.
In 1653 Cromwell dissolved this parliament, an extension of the Long Parliament. It was formed in 1648 under Cromwell's control and ordered the trial and subsequent execution of Charles I.
